newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bp to 10.3 pct.
newsitem.headline: Croatian lending rate rises 70 bp to 10.3 pct.

text.p: The Croatian average lending rate edged up 70 basis points to 10.3 percent on Wednesday, lifted by the increased volume of renewed term loans.
Supply stood at 72 million kuna, unchanged from Tuesday, overshooting demand by more than 32 million kuna.
Dealers put total daily settlements at 37.4 million kuna, most of which were extended interbank loans ranging between 7.0 percent for call money to 13 percent for one-month loans.
Fresh trade amounted to a modest 13.2 million kuna of which 13 million were call money loans granted at a steady 8.0 percent. One small 32-day new loan was granted to a savings bank at 16 percent.
The central bank calculated its kuna midrates for Thursday firmer at 6.3864 from 6.4008 to the dollar and slightly firmer at 3.5650 from 3.5679 versus the German mark. -- Laura Lui, 385-1-4557075
